# AtlasTooLargeException

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Publish` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public sealed class AtlasTooLargeException : InvalidOperationException
```

A Menu atlas would be larger than one image can be (a pixel ceiling on a side, or in area), so the write is refused rather than built.

## Remarks

The refusal carries its two halves separately. [`AtlasTooLargeException.Problem`](Nfty.Core.Publish.AtlasTooLargeException.md#p-problem) is what is wrong and is true on any front-end; [`AtlasTooLargeException.Hint`](Nfty.Core.Publish.AtlasTooLargeException.md#p-hint) is the way out spelled for the command line. The CLI prints `Message`, which joins them, so its text is what it always was. A screen with its own Atlas/Loose tray shows [`AtlasTooLargeException.Problem`](Nfty.Core.Publish.AtlasTooLargeException.md#p-problem) and says "Choose Loose" in its own words, instead of leaking a flag that does not exist there.

It derives from `InvalidOperationException` because that is what the refusal threw before it had a type, so any caller that caught the base keeps working.
